family: per-paper nondimensionalization (problem-specific scaling / "code units" / reduced units)

systems.name: Inertial (convective) scaling of the incompressible Navier–Stokes equations
systems.used_in: fluid mechanics, turbulence, aerodynamics, geophysical fluid dynamics; the default nondimensionalization in almost every incompressible-flow paper

per_symbol_rescalings.relation: p_\text{phys} = \rho U^2\,\hat p  (some papers use p/(\rho U^2) + gz absorbed, or \hat p = (p-p_\infty)/(\tfrac12\rho U^2) = C_p)
per_symbol_rescalings.why: pressure has no independent scale; it is slaved to \rho U^2, and the engineering convention inserts a factor 1/2 (pressure coefficient) that dimensional analysis cannot see

per_symbol_rescalings.relation: \nu is NOT a generator; it survives as 1/Re = \nu/(UL)
per_symbol_rescalings.why: only three scales are independent in (M,L,T); \nu is the residue. A paper that says "we set L=U=\nu=1" has silently imposed Re=1, a physical restriction, not a unit choice.

fingerprints: "where lengths are scaled by L, velocities by U and time by L/U"; "hats denote dimensionless quantities"
displayed momentum equation with a bare 1/Re (or Re^{-1}) multiplying \nabla^2 u and coefficient 1 on the advective term
phrases "unit box", "domain [0,1]^3", "we drop the hats henceforth"
a Table 1 of "reference quantities" with rows length/velocity/time/pressure

benchmark_equations.coulomb: N/A: no electromagnetic content in the incompressible NS system.
benchmark_equations.gauss_law: N/A: no electromagnetic content; the only divergence constraint is the incompressibility condition \nabla\cdot\hat u = 0.

systems.notes: Rank-3 generator set over (M,L,T); Θ and I inactive. This is the cleanest test case that the generator formalism extends to user-declared scales: L, U, ρ are dimensionally independent, so the restoration linear system is uniquely solvable exactly as for ħ=c=1. The essential new feature versus fixed unit systems is the RESIDUE: 1/Re is a dimensionless group that must NOT be restored — it is part of the equation. The tool needs a hard distinction between "absorbed generator" and "surviving dimensionless group".

systems.name: Viscous (diffusive/Stokes) scaling of the incompressible Navier–Stokes equations
systems.used_in: microhydrodynamics, suspension mechanics, Stokes-flow and lubrication theory, low-Re swimming, and the linear-stability literature (Orr–Sommerfeld in viscous units)

per_symbol_rescalings.relation: t_\text{phys} = (L^2/\nu)\,\hat t  instead of (L/U)\,\hat t
per_symbol_rescalings.why: same problem, different time generator; a reader who assumes convective time units misreads every reported growth rate by a factor Re

per_symbol_rescalings.relation: p_\text{phys} = (\rho\nu U/L)\,\hat p = (\mu U/L)\hat p
per_symbol_rescalings.why: viscous rather than dynamic pressure scale

fingerprints: "time is measured in viscous units L^2/\nu" / "viscous time" / "diffusive time scale"

abla u) = -

abla^2 u  (Re multiplying the LHS, coefficient 1 on the Laplacian)
Stokes limit displayed as 0 = -\nabla \hat p + \nabla^2\hat u
wall units u^+, y^+, t^+ with u_\tau and \nu/u_\tau (the near-wall variant of this scaling)

benchmark_equations.coulomb: N/A: no electromagnetic content.
benchmark_equations.gauss_law: N/A: only \nabla\cdot\hat u = 0.

systems.notes:
Dimensionally this is the SAME generator lattice as the inertial scaling with U replaced by 
u/L; the tool must treat them as distinct named presets because the numerical values reported in papers differ by powers of Re. Wall units (u_	au, 
u/u_	au,

systems.name: Compressible / aerodynamic (Mach) nondimensionalization
systems.used_in: compressible CFD, aeroacoustics, high-speed aerodynamics, shock-capturing scheme papers

per_symbol_rescalings.relation: \hat p = p/(\rho_\infty a_\infty^2)  \Rightarrow  \hat p_\infty = 1/\gamma ;  alternative \hat p = p/(\gamma p_\infty) \Rightarrow \hat p_\infty = 1/\gamma ; alternative \hat p = p/p_\infty \Rightarrow \hat p_\infty = 1
per_symbol_rescalings.why: three incompatible pressure normalizations are all called "nondimensional pressure"; they differ by the dimensionless factor \gamma, which no dimensional check can catch

per_symbol_rescalings.relation: \hat T = T/T_\infty with \hat e = \hat p/((\gamma-1)\hat\rho); some papers scale T by U_\infty^2/c_p instead
per_symbol_rescalings.why: the temperature generator is either T_\infty or the recovery temperature; the two differ by (\gamma-1)M^2/2

fingerprints: "freestream conditions are used as reference: \rho_\infty, a_\infty, L"
residues M_\infty (or Ma), Re, Pr, \gamma appearing simultaneously in the displayed viscous flux
energy equation carrying (\gamma-1)M_\infty^2 or \gamma/(Pr\,Re) coefficients
statements like "the nondimensional freestream pressure is 1/\gamma"

benchmark_equations.coulomb: N/A: neutral gas dynamics.
benchmark_equations.gauss_law: N/A: no EM content.

systems.notes: Θ becomes an active basis dimension here (unlike most of this family, which sets k_B=1 and kills Θ). The 1/\gamma pressure trap is the single most common source of misread CFD initial conditions and is invisible to dimension checking — it belongs in numeric_factor/emits bookkeeping.

systems.name: Boussinesq free-fall (buoyancy) scaling
systems.used_in: turbulent Rayleigh–Bénard convection, mantle/stellar convection simulations, most DNS papers with Ra > 10^6

per_symbol_rescalings.relation: t_\text{phys} = (H/U_f)\,\hat t = \tau_f \hat t ; free-fall time \tau_f = H/\sqrt{g\alpha\Delta T H}
per_symbol_rescalings.why: papers quote averaging windows and Nusselt convergence in "free-fall times"; converting requires \tau_f, not H^2/\kappa

per_symbol_rescalings.relation: \hat\theta = (T - T_\text{ref})/\Delta T with T_\text{ref} = (T_\text{top}+T_\text{bot})/2 in most papers, but T_\text{top} in others
per_symbol_rescalings.why: an additive offset, not a scaling — outside the multiplicative generator formalism entirely

fingerprints: explicit coefficients \sqrt{Pr/Ra} on the viscous term and 1/\sqrt{Ra\,Pr} on the thermal-diffusion term
"free-fall velocity", "free-fall time units", "\tau_f"

systems.name: Boussinesq diffusive (thermal) scaling
systems.used_in: linear stability theory of convection, onset/bifurcation studies, mantle convection, and older RBC literature; still standard in Ra ≲ 10^6 work

per_symbol_rescalings.relation: \hat u = u/(\kappa/H)  (velocity scale is \kappa/H, not U_f); \hat u_\text{diff} = \sqrt{Ra\,Pr}\;\hat u_\text{free-fall}
per_symbol_rescalings.why: the two RBC conventions differ by \sqrt{Ra Pr} in every reported velocity, Reynolds number and spectrum amplitude

per_symbol_rescalings.relation: t_\text{phys} = (H^2/\kappa)\hat t ; some authors use the VISCOUS diffusive time H^2/\nu instead
per_symbol_rescalings.why: a third choice inside the same 'diffusive scaling' label, differing by Pr

benchmark_equations.coulomb: N/A: no EM content.
benchmark_equations.gauss_law: N/A: only \nabla\cdot\hat u = 0.

systems.notes: This entry exists to prove a structural point: two papers on IDENTICAL physics declare different generator sets, and the only textual discriminator is which dimensionless group sits on which term. A units-translation tool must be able to translate BETWEEN two per-paper conventions, not just to/from SI — the composite map is a power of Ra and Pr on each symbol.

systems.name: Periodic-box spectral units
systems.used_in: homogeneous isotropic turbulence DNS, MHD turbulence, spectral-method papers, lattice-free field simulations

per_symbol_rescalings.relation: box of side 2\pi \Rightarrow k \in \mathbb{Z}^3 ; box of side 1 \Rightarrow k \in 2\pi\mathbb{Z}^3
per_symbol_rescalings.why: the 2\pi is a pure numeric factor and is exactly the kind of thing dimensional analysis cannot recover; energy spectra E(k), k_\text{max}\eta, and the Kolmogorov constant all shift

per_symbol_rescalings.relation: \int E(k)\,dk = \tfrac12\langle u^2\rangle in both conventions, but the shell-binning \Delta k = 1 differs from \Delta k = 2\pi/L
per_symbol_rescalings.why: reported spectral amplitudes differ by 2\pi even when the physics is identical

fingerprints: "in a periodic box of size 2\pi" / "[0,2\pi]^3" / "the box size is set to unity"
"wavenumbers are integers" / "k_\text{min} = 1"
forcing described as "applied in the shell 1 \le |k| \le 2"
resolution quoted as k_\text{max}\eta \ge 1.5 (a residue that is convention-independent)

benchmark_equations.coulomb: N/A: no EM content in the hydrodynamic case; in the MHD case see the Alfvénic-units entry.
benchmark_equations.gauss_law: N/A: constraints are \nabla\cdot\hat u = 0 and (MHD) \nabla\cdot\hat B = 0.

systems.notes: The 2\pi ambiguity here is the direct analogue of the ħ-versus-h ambiguity in natural units: same dimension, different numeric factor. This is strong evidence that numeric_factor must be a first-class field for user-declared generators too, not just for the fixed systems.

systems.name: MHD Alfvénic code units
systems.used_in: solar/space physics, MHD turbulence, reconnection studies, fusion MHD codes (JOREK, PLUTO, Athena, BATS-R-US)

per_symbol_rescalings.relation: B_\text{code} = B_\text{SI}/\sqrt{\mu_0\rho_0} (velocity units) or B_\text{code} = B_\text{Gauss}/\sqrt{4\pi\rho_0}
per_symbol_rescalings.why: most MHD codes store B in velocity units so that v_A = B; the magnetic pressure then reads B^2/2, not B^2/8\pi or B^2/2\mu_0. This is a genuine symbol redefinition on top of the quotient.

per_symbol_rescalings.relation: \hat p = p/(B_0^2/\mu_0) \Rightarrow \beta = 2\hat p/\hat B^2 ; alternative \hat p = p/(\rho_0 v_A^2) is identical, but \hat p = p/p_0 is not
per_symbol_rescalings.why: pressure is slaved to the magnetic scale in one convention and independent in the other; \beta gets a factor 2 wrong if confused

per_symbol_rescalings.relation: t_\text{phys} = (L_0/v_A)\hat t, v_A = B_0/\sqrt{\mu_0\rho_0}
per_symbol_rescalings.why: 'Alfvén times' vs 'Alfvén crossing times' vs 'sound crossing times' are quoted interchangeably in the solar literature

fingerprints: "velocities are normalized to the Alfvén speed v_A = B_0/\sqrt{4\pi\rho_0}" (Gaussian) or "B_0/\sqrt{\mu_0\rho_0}" (SI)
induction equation with 1/S (Lundquist number) on the resistive term: \partial_t B = \nabla\times(v\times B) + S^{-1}\nabla^2 B
total pressure written as (p + B^2/2) with no \mu_0 or 8\pi anywhere
"time is measured in Alfvén times \tau_A = L_0/v_A"
residues S, Re_m, Pr_m = \nu/\eta, \beta, M_A

benchmark_equations.coulomb: N/A: quasineutral MHD; no explicit Coulomb potential appears.
benchmark_equations.gauss_law: Electric Gauss law is dropped (quasineutrality). The retained constraint is \nabla\cdot\hat B = 0, with Ampère's law reduced to \hat J = \nabla\times\hat B (displacement current dropped, \mu_0 absorbed).
benchmark_equations.einstein_field: N/A: nonrelativistic MHD. (GRMHD codes stack these normalizations on top of G=c=1 — see the GRMHD entry.)

systems.notes: Four declared scales but only three independent dimensions once I is eliminated by absorbing \mu_0 — i.e. \mu_0 = 1 is what removes the current dimension from the basis, exactly as k_B = 1 removes Θ. This is the clearest example in the family of a per-paper declaration performing a BASIS REDUCTION rather than a mere scaling, and the tool needs to model that explicitly.

systems.name: Gyrokinetic normalization, GENE / c_s family
systems.used_in: tokamak/stellarator microturbulence (GENE, GENE-X, GKW, ORB5, GX, CGYRO with its own variant)

per_symbol_rescalings.relation: \phi = (T_\text{ref}/e)\,\hat\phi in global GENE; local (flux-tube, \delta f) codes carry an extra \rho^*: \phi = (T_\text{ref}\rho^*/e)\hat\phi
per_symbol_rescalings.why: in the local limit fluctuation amplitudes are O(\rho^*) by the gyrokinetic ordering, so the field normalization differs between the local and global versions of the SAME code

per_symbol_rescalings.relation: A_\parallel = \rho_\text{ref}B_\text{ref}\hat A_\parallel
per_symbol_rescalings.why: the parallel vector potential is normalized with a gyroradius, not L_ref — a mixed-scale normalization that a naive quotient reconstruction gets wrong by \rho^*

per_symbol_rescalings.relation: k_\perp\rho_\text{ref} = O(1) but k_\parallel L_\text{ref} = O(1)
per_symbol_rescalings.why: the gyrokinetic ordering means perpendicular and parallel lengths use DIFFERENT length generators; a single L in the generator table is insufficient

per_symbol_rescalings.relation: \beta_\text{ref} = 8\pi n_\text{ref}T_\text{ref}/B_\text{ref}^2 (Gaussian-rooted, GENE) vs 2\mu_0 nT/B^2 (SI-rooted)
per_symbol_rescalings.why: factor-of-4\pi discrepancy in the electromagnetic residue

fingerprints: "c_s = \sqrt{T_e/m_i}" together with "\rho_s = c_s/\Omega_i"
time normalized as L_\text{ref}/c_\text{ref}; growth rates quoted as \gamma (c_s/a) or \gamma (c_s/R)
gradients quoted as R/L_{T_i} or a/L_n; heat flux quoted in gyro-Bohm units Q_\text{gB} = n T c_s \rho_s^2/L^2
\rho^* = \rho_\text{ref}/L_\text{ref} appearing as an explicit small parameter
"\beta_\text{ref} = 8\pi n_\text{ref}T_\text{ref}/B_\text{ref}^2"

benchmark_equations.coulomb: N/A: the Coulomb interaction enters only through a collision operator and through quasineutrality; no bare Coulomb potential is displayed.
benchmark_equations.gauss_law: Poisson's equation is REPLACED by gyrokinetic quasineutrality: \sum_s \hat q_s\big(\int \hat f_s\,d^3\hat v - \hat n_s\hat q_s\hat\phi/\hat T_s\big) = 0, i.e. \sum_s \hat q_s \hat n_{1s} = 0 with a polarization-density term. The Debye term (\lambda_D/\rho_s)^2\nabla^2\hat\phi is retained only in codes with an explicit 'Debye length' input.

systems.notes: Two independent per-paper choices sit INSIDE this single named convention: (i) L_ref = major radius R_0 vs minor radius a (a factor of the aspect ratio in every quoted gradient and growth rate), and (ii) T_ref = T_e vs T_i. Both are runtime switches, not code identities, so the tool cannot infer them from the code name alone. The local/global \rho^* field normalization difference is stated at moderate confidence — I verified the global-GENE form (\psi_{1\alpha} = T_\text{ref}\hat\psi_{1\alpha}/e, A_\parallel = \rho_\text{ref}B_\text{ref}\hat A_\parallel) from the global-GENE paper but inferred the local-code \rho^* factor from the gyrokinetic ordering rather than reading it off a source.

systems.name: Gyrokinetic normalization, GS2 / stella / AstroGK family
systems.used_in: GS2, stella, AstroGK, and the astrophysical-gyrokinetics literature (Howes et al.)

per_symbol_rescalings.relation: v_{t,\text{GS2}} = \sqrt{2T/m} = \sqrt{2}\,v_{th,\text{GENE-style}} ; but the NORMALIZED thermal speed inside the code is \hat v_{th}=\sqrt{\hat T/\hat m}, i.e. \sqrt{T/m} without the 2
per_symbol_rescalings.why: GS2's own documentation warns that the reference-species normalization strips the \sqrt{2}, so the same symbol v_th means different things inside and outside the code; growth rates differ by \sqrt{2}

per_symbol_rescalings.relation: \rho_{r} = v_{t,r}/\Omega_r = \sqrt{2}\,\rho_{s,\text{GENE-style}}
per_symbol_rescalings.why: every quoted k_\perp\rho spectrum peak shifts by \sqrt{2} between the two families — the single most common cross-code comparison error in gyrokinetics

per_symbol_rescalings.relation: \gamma_\text{GS2} in units v_{t}/a ; \gamma_\text{GENE} in units c_s/L_\text{ref}
per_symbol_rescalings.why: combined \sqrt{2} and R/a factors

fingerprints: "v_t = \sqrt{2T/m}" appearing explicitly in a normalization table
frequencies quoted in units of v_{t,i}/a; wavenumbers as k_y\rho_i with \rho_i = v_{t,i}/\Omega_i
"reference species" language; "tprim", "fprim", "vnewk" (GS2 input-file keywords leaking into the text)
astrophysical variants quoting k_\perp\rho_i across the ion-Larmor transition

benchmark_equations.coulomb: N/A: enters only through the collision operator.
benchmark_equations.gauss_law: Gyrokinetic quasineutrality \sum_s \hat q_s \hat n_{1s} = 0 with polarization, as in the GENE family; the \sqrt{2} sits in the velocity integrals, not in the field equation's form.

systems.notes: This is the single best real-world argument in this family for keeping numeric_factor separate from dimension: GS2 and GENE have IDENTICAL generator dimensions and differ only by \sqrt{2} in the velocity generator. A tool that dimension-checks only will declare the two conventions identical and silently produce results wrong by powers of \sqrt{2}. Verified against the GS2 user manual's normalisations page.

systems.name: PIC / kinetic-plasma normalized units
systems.used_in: particle-in-cell simulations of laser-plasma interaction, collisionless shocks, magnetic reconnection, astrophysical kinetic plasma

per_symbol_rescalings.relation: \hat E = eE/(m_ec\omega_{pe}) ; laser-plasma papers instead use a_0 = eE/(m_ec\omega_L) with the LASER frequency
per_symbol_rescalings.why: two different frequency generators for the same field symbol; a_0 = 1 is the relativistic-intensity threshold, not a unit choice

per_symbol_rescalings.relation: \hat B = eB/(m_e\omega_{pe}) (so that \hat B = \hat E for a light wave); alternatively normalized to \omega_{ce}
per_symbol_rescalings.why: the magnetization residue \sigma = B^2/(4\pi n m c^2) or \omega_{ce}/\omega_{pe} depends on which is chosen

per_symbol_rescalings.relation: \hat p = p/(m_ec) — momentum, not velocity, is normalized, because the code is relativistic
per_symbol_rescalings.why: reported 'velocities' > 1 are four-velocities; a naive v/c reading is wrong

fingerprints: "lengths are in units of the electron skin depth c/\omega_{pe}" or "d_e", "d_i"
"time in units of \omega_{pe}^{-1}" / "\Omega_{ci}^{-1}"
Maxwell equations displayed with all constants gone: \partial_t E = \nabla\times B - J, \nabla\cdot E = \rho
normalized vector potential a_0 quoted for laser intensity; "m_i/m_e = 25" (reduced mass ratio) as a residue
magnetization \sigma, plasma \beta, \omega_{pe}/\omega_{ce} appearing as the surviving parameters

benchmark_equations.coulomb: Rarely displayed; the implied form is \hat U = \hat q_1\hat q_2/(4\pi \hat r) in SI-rooted normalization or \hat q_1\hat q_2/\hat r in Gaussian-rooted normalization. Papers essentially never write it, so this is a weak fingerprint.
benchmark_equations.gauss_law:
abla\cdot\hat E = \hatho — derived here: with \hat x = x\omega_{pe}/c, \hat E = eE/(m_ec\omega_{pe}), \hat n = n/n_0, the SI law 
abla\cdot E = en/\varepsilon_0 becomes (m_e\omega_{pe}^2/e)
abla\!\cdot\!\hat E = e n_0\hat n/\varepsilon_0 = m_e\omega_{pe}^2\hat n, i.e. 
abla\cdot\hat E = \hat n exactly, with no residual 4\pi.
benchmark_equations.einstein_field: N/A for standard PIC; GRPIC codes stack G=c=1 on top (see numerical-relativity entry).
benchmark_equations.schrodinger_or_dirac: N/A: classical Vlasov–Maxwell (QED-PIC modules reintroduce \hbar and \alpha explicitly as residues).

systems.notes: The \varepsilon_0/4\pi bookkeeping is fully absorbed because \omega_{pe} itself contains it — the derivation above shows the 4\pi cancels identically. The nastiest real trap is the reduced mass ratio m_i/m_e (25, 64, 100 instead of 1836): a dimensionless residue deliberately set to an unphysical value, which no dimension check can flag and which a restoration engine must never 'restore' to 1836.

systems.name: Numerical-relativity code units (G = c = M = 1)
aliases: geometrized units with a mass scale
systems.used_in: binary black hole and binary neutron star simulations, waveform catalogs (SXS, RIT, MAYA), initial-data codes, TOV solvers

per_symbol_rescalings.relation: 1\,M_\odot \equiv GM_\odot/c^2 = 1.47662\ \text{km} = GM_\odot/c^3 = 4.92549\times10^{-6}\ \text{s}
per_symbol_rescalings.why: 'M' is used simultaneously as a mass, a length and a time in the same paper; the reader must supply the mass scale to disambiguate

per_symbol_rescalings.relation: \rho_\text{unit} = c^6/(G^3M_\odot^2) \approx 6.18\times10^{17}\ \text{g\,cm}^{-3} (so the standard TOV test \rho_c = 1.28\times10^{-3} is \approx 7.9\times10^{14}\ \text{g\,cm}^{-3})
per_symbol_rescalings.why: matter simulations quote densities in code units that look like small numbers; restoring them requires the mass scale, which is NOT free once an EOS is fixed

per_symbol_rescalings.relation: waveforms published as (D/M)h_{+,\times} versus (t-r_*)/M
per_symbol_rescalings.why: the M=1 generator is exactly the scale symmetry of vacuum GR, so vacuum waveforms are genuinely mass-independent; this is why the declaration is legitimate there and illegitimate with matter

fingerprints: "we use geometrized units G = c = 1" followed by "and set the total mass M = 1"
masses quoted as m_1 = m_2 = 0.5, or "the initial separation is D = 11M"
times and radii carrying an explicit trailing M: "t = 1000M", "r = 100M"
"in units of M_\odot" for matter runs; \rho_c \sim 10^{-3}, K = 100 (polytropic constant) as tell-tale code-unit numbers
conversion appendix listing 1.4766 km and 4.9255 \mu s

benchmark_equations.coulomb: N/A in vacuum NR. In force-free/GRMHD extensions the Gaussian-rooted form is used with \mu_0 or 4\pi additionally absorbed — see the GRMHD entry.
benchmark_equations.gauss_law: The gravitational analogue actually solved is the Hamiltonian constraint R + K^2 - K_{ij}K^{ij} = 16\pi\rho (G=c=1), and the momentum constraint D_j(K^{ij}-\gamma^{ij}K) = 8\pi S^i. The M=1 generator leaves both coefficient-unchanged.
benchmark_equations.einstein_field: G_{ab} = 8\pi T_{ab}. The M = 1 declaration emits NOTHING here: it is the exact scale symmetry g_{ab}(x)\to g_{ab}(x/\lambda), (M,t,r)\to\lambda(M,t,r), T_{ab}\to\lambda^{-2}T_{ab} of the vacuum field equations, so the equation form is identical to plain geometrized units. This is the one case in the whole family where a declared generator has no equation-level consequence.

systems.notes: CRITICAL interaction with the fixed geometrized system: G=c=1 leaves a one-parameter residual scaling freedom (a single remaining dimension, usually called 'mass'), and M=1 fixes it. So NR code units are geometrized units PLUS one custom generator, i.e. the generator table composes: fixed generators + user generators, with the user generator's dimension chosen to complete the basis. The physics trap: for VACUUM (BBH) the mass scale is genuinely free and results are universal; with MATTER (BNS, an EOS with its own density scale) the mass scale is NOT free, and 'M=1' means 'M = M_phys/M_scale', a reported number, not a symmetry. The tool should warn when a matter EOS is present alongside an M=1 declaration.

systems.name: Astrophysical simulation code-unit triples (G ≠ 1)
systems.used_in: cosmological N-body and hydro simulations (GADGET, AREPO, RAMSES, GIZMO), galactic dynamics, star-cluster simulations, ISM codes (FLASH, Athena++)

per_symbol_rescalings.relation: G_\text{code} = G\,[M]/([L][V]^2) = 43007.1 for (\mathrm{kpc}/h,\ 10^{10}M_\odot/h,\ \mathrm{km\,s^{-1}}) — the h factors cancel
per_symbol_rescalings.why: THE central counterexample in this family: the declared generators do NOT set G=1. A restoration engine that assumes 'code units ⇒ G=1' is simply wrong for the most widely used astrophysics codes.

per_symbol_rescalings.relation: [T] = [L]/[V] = 0.978\ \mathrm{Gyr}/h for the Gadget triple
per_symbol_rescalings.why: the derived time unit is never declared explicitly and must be computed from the triple

per_symbol_rescalings.relation: comoving vs physical: x_\text{phys} = a\,x_\text{com}, and Gadget's internal velocity variable carries an extra \sqrt{a}
per_symbol_rescalings.why: a time-dependent rescaling — outside the constant-generator formalism altogether

fingerprints: a table "UnitLength_in_cm / UnitMass_in_g / UnitVelocity_in_cm_per_s"
"masses are in units of 10^{10}\,M_\odot/h", "lengths in ckpc/h"
the literal number 43007.1 or 43009 appearing as G in a methods section or parameter file
"comoving coordinates", "internal velocity variable", "\sqrt{a} factor"

benchmark_equations.coulomb: N/A: gravity-only or MHD; see the Alfvénic entry for the magnetic sector.
benchmark_equations.gauss_law: Poisson's equation retains G explicitly: \nabla^2\Phi = 4\pi G_\text{code}\,\rho, with G_\text{code} = 43007.1 rather than 1.
benchmark_equations.schrodinger_or_dirac: N/A, except in fuzzy-dark-matter codes which additionally declare \hbar/m as a single generator (a length^2/time).

systems.notes: This entry is the reason the tool must not conflate 'code units' with 'natural units'. A code-unit declaration is a pure change of numerical scale with NO constants absorbed; every physical constant survives with a nontrivial numeric value. The generator table handles it fine — the generators are (L, M, V) with numeric values in SI — but the UI must accept generators whose absorbed constant list is EMPTY.

systems.name: GRMHD code units (G = c = M = 1 plus an independent density/accretion scale)
aliases: code units with a free mass-accretion scale
systems.used_in: black-hole accretion simulations (HARM, KORAL, BHAC, H-AMR), EHT-related radiative transfer, jet launching

per_symbol_rescalings.relation: B_\text{code} = B_\text{Gauss}/\sqrt{4\pi} (Heaviside-like absorption), so magnetic pressure is b^2/2 and \beta = 2p/b^2
per_symbol_rescalings.why: the same \sqrt{4\pi} redefinition as in Newtonian MHD codes, stacked on top of geometrized units

per_symbol_rescalings.relation: \rho_\text{phys} = \mathcal{M}_\text{unit}/L_\text{unit}^3 \times \rho_\text{code}, L_\text{unit} = GM_\text{BH}/c^2
per_symbol_rescalings.why: ideal GRMHD is scale-free in density, so the density scale is set only in post-processing (fixed by matching an observed flux); the SAME simulation is published at several \mathcal{M}_\text{unit} values

fingerprints: "the simulations are scale-free in density; we set the mass unit in post-processing"
"M_\text{unit}", "\mathcal{M}_\text{unit}", "the density scale is fixed by matching the 230 GHz flux"
r_g = GM/c^2, t_g = GM/c^3; times quoted as "t = 10^4\,r_g/c"
\sigma = b^2/\rho, \beta = 2p/b^2 as the surviving parameters; "\sigma_\text{cut}"

benchmark_equations.coulomb: N/A: ideal MHD, quasineutral.
benchmark_equations.gauss_law:
abla_\mu {}^*F^{\mu
u} = 0 (no magnetic monopoles) with the 4\pi absorbed; electric Gauss law is not solved (ideal-MHD condition u_\mu F^{\mu
u} = 0 replaces it).
benchmark_equations.einstein_field: G_{ab} = 8\pi T_{ab} in the Cowling/fixed-Kerr approximation the metric is prescribed and this is not solved; when it is (dynamical GRMHD), the coefficient is 8\pi exactly as in geometrized units.

systems.notes: Structurally interesting: TWO mass generators are declared (M_BH and \mathcal{M}_unit) even though they have identical dimensions. That is only consistent because the equations have an exact density-scaling symmetry in ideal GRMHD — the second 'generator' is really a symmetry parameter. A rank check on dimensions alone would flag this as over-determined and would be wrong. The tool needs a concept of 'generator that exploits a symmetry of the equations' distinct from 'generator that fixes a unit'.

systems.name: Shearing-box / accretion-disk units (Ω = 1)
systems.used_in: MRI and disk-turbulence simulations, planet-formation and dust-settling studies, protoplanetary disk microphysics

per_symbol_rescalings.relation: "orbits" = 2\pi/\Omega, "shear times" = 1/(q\Omega), "\Omega^{-1}" — three time units in the same literature
per_symbol_rescalings.why: the 2\pi is a pure numeric factor; a run reported as '100 orbits' is 628 \Omega^{-1}

per_symbol_rescalings.relation: H = c_s/\Omega (isothermal) vs H = \sqrt{2}c_s/\Omega (Gaussian-profile convention)
per_symbol_rescalings.why: factor-\sqrt{2} disagreement in the scale-height definition propagates into every quoted box size

fingerprints: "we adopt the shearing-box approximation with \Omega = 1"; "q = -d\ln\Omega/d\ln R = 3/2"
box dimensions quoted in H: "L_x \times L_y \times L_z = 4H\times 8H \times 4H"
times quoted in "orbits" or "\Omega^{-1}"
residues: \alpha (Shakura–Sunyaev), \beta_\text{plasma}, Stokes number St = \tau_s\Omega, Elsasser number

benchmark_equations.coulomb: N/A.
benchmark_equations.gauss_law: \nabla\cdot\hat B = 0; magnetic units follow the Alfvénic convention (\mu_0 or 4\pi absorbed).
benchmark_equations.einstein_field: N/A: Newtonian, with tidal expansion of the potential -q\Omega^2x^2 + \tfrac12\Omega^2z^2.

systems.notes: The Stokes number St = \tau_s\Omega is a residue that looks like a unit statement ('we set the stopping time to 0.1') but is a physical parameter. Confusing the two is a common misreading of dust-dynamics papers.

systems.name: Hénon (N-body standard) units
systems.used_in: collisional stellar dynamics, globular-cluster and star-cluster N-body simulations, and the direct-N-body code literature (NBODY6, PeTar)

per_symbol_rescalings.relation: virial radius R_v \equiv GM^2/(-2W) = 1 exactly, given the virial theorem W = 2E = -1/2
per_symbol_rescalings.why: the E = -1/4 numeric choice exists precisely to make R_v = 1; the '-1/4' is a pure numeric factor invisible to dimensional analysis

per_symbol_rescalings.relation: crossing time t_\text{cr} = 2R_v/v_\text{rms} = 2\sqrt{2} \approx 2.828 N-body time units
per_symbol_rescalings.why: derived here: T = -E = 1/4 = \tfrac12 M v_\text{rms}^2 with M=1 gives v_\text{rms} = 1/\sqrt{2}, so t_\text{cr} = 2\sqrt2. Papers quote both 'N-body times' and 'crossing times'.

per_symbol_rescalings.relation: individual particle masses m_i = 1/N
per_symbol_rescalings.why: a further dimensionless choice; some papers instead set m_i = 1 and M = N

fingerprints: "we use N-body units (Hénon units) in which G = M = 1 and E = -1/4"
"the virial radius is unity"; "times are given in N-body units"
the number 2\sqrt{2} or 2.83 as a crossing time
relaxation times quoted as t_\text{rh} \propto N/\ln(\gamma N) in N-body units

benchmark_equations.coulomb: N/A: gravitational N-body only. (Formally identical 1/r structure with G\,m_im_j replacing q_iq_j/4\pi\varepsilon_0.)
benchmark_equations.gauss_law: \nabla^2\Phi = 4\pi\rho with G absorbed.
benchmark_equations.einstein_field: N/A: Newtonian (post-Newtonian terms, when included, reintroduce c explicitly as a residue c \approx 3\times10^5 in the code's velocity unit — an easy-to-miss dimensional leak).

systems.notes: Dimensionally independent: the 3x3 exponent matrix for (G, M, E) has determinant 2, so the generator set is complete and the restoration system is uniquely solvable. The -1/4 is the numeric_factor. I verified R_v = 1 and t_cr = 2\sqrt2 by direct derivation from the virial theorem rather than from a source; confidence high but the source citation is indirect. Worth noting the historical sibling: the astronomical system based on the Gaussian gravitational constant k = 0.01720209895, in which GM_\odot = k^2\,\mathrm{AU}^3\,\mathrm{day}^{-2} — a per-field scaling that defined the AU until the 2012 IAU redefinition.

systems.name: Lennard-Jones reduced (molecular-dynamics) units
systems.used_in: molecular dynamics and Monte Carlo of simple liquids, glass-formers, colloids, polymer coarse-graining; the LAMMPS/GROMACS/HOOMD 'lj' unit setting

per_symbol_rescalings.relation: \tau = \sqrt{m\sigma^2/\varepsilon} ; t^* = t/\tau
per_symbol_rescalings.why: the derived time unit is never a declared generator but is the quantity every reported timestep (\Delta t^* = 0.005) refers to

per_symbol_rescalings.relation: T^* = k_BT/\varepsilon
per_symbol_rescalings.why: once k_B = 1 the Θ dimension is eliminated from the basis; 'temperature' in the paper is an energy

per_symbol_rescalings.relation: P^* = P\sigma^3/\varepsilon
per_symbol_rescalings.why: derived, not declared

per_symbol_rescalings.relation: \rho^* = N\sigma^3/V (number density, NOT mass density)
per_symbol_rescalings.why: the asterisked density in MD papers is a number density even though \rho denotes mass density elsewhere in physics

fingerprints: "units lj" (a LAMMPS input line quoted in the methods)
U(r) = 4\varepsilon[(\sigma/r)^{12}-(\sigma/r)^6] written with \varepsilon = \sigma = 1, i.e. U^*(r^*) = 4(r^{*-12}-r^{*-6})
starred variables T^*, \rho^*, P^*, t^* with a 'reduced units' sentence
cutoff quoted as r_c = 2.5 (in \sigma); LJ triple point \rho^*\approx0.84, T^*\approx0.69
"in argon units, \sigma = 3.4\ \text{Å}, \varepsilon/k_B = 120\ \text{K}" as the restoration recipe

benchmark_equations.coulomb: N/A for the neutral LJ system; charged variants use the reduced form \beta u_C(r) = \ell_B q_iq_j/r with the Bjerrum length \ell_B = e^2/(4\pi\varepsilon_0\varepsilon_r k_BT) measured in \sigma — see the soft-matter entry.
benchmark_equations.gauss_law: N/A: no field equations are solved (pairwise forces only); Ewald/PPPM solvers reintroduce 4\pi\varepsilon_0 through a single prefactor constant.
benchmark_equations.schrodinger_or_dirac: N/A: classical MD. Path-integral MD reintroduces \hbar as an explicit residue \hbar^*=\hbar/\sqrt{m\sigma^2\varepsilon} (the de Boer parameter \Lambda^*).

systems.notes: Four generators over four active dimensions (M, L, T, Θ) — a complete, dimensionally independent set, so restoration is unique. This is the textbook case that the generator formalism extends verbatim to user-declared scales. Note that k_B = 1 here performs the same basis reduction as in thermal-field-theory natural units; the tool's Θ-elimination logic can be shared. Verified against the LAMMPS units documentation.

systems.name: Soft-matter / coarse-grained reduced units with electrostatics
systems.used_in: polyelectrolyte and colloid simulation, dissipative particle dynamics, implicit-solvent electrostatics, coarse-grained DNA/protein models

per_symbol_rescalings.relation: charges in units of e, with the entire electrostatic prefactor carried by \ell_B = e^2/(4\pi\varepsilon_0\varepsilon_rk_BT); \beta u(r) = \ell_B q_iq_j/r
per_symbol_rescalings.why: the paper's only electrostatic 'unit' is a LENGTH (the Bjerrum length), so the charge dimension I is eliminated entirely — a basis reduction, not a rescaling

per_symbol_rescalings.relation: energy scale is k_BT itself, so temperature never appears; instead \ell_B/\sigma is the control parameter
per_symbol_rescalings.why: the temperature dependence is folded into a length ratio, which makes T-dependence invisible in the equations

per_symbol_rescalings.relation: screening enters as \kappa^2 = 4\pi\ell_B\sum_i q_i^2 n_i (Debye–Hückel), with the 4\pi explicit
per_symbol_rescalings.why: a surviving 4\pi that a rationalization-blind converter will misplace

fingerprints: "energies are measured in units of k_BT"; "the Bjerrum length is \ell_B = 0.7\ \text{nm} = 1.4\sigma"
\beta u(r) = \ell_B/r appearing as the Coulomb interaction
DPD: "a_{ij} = 25" (the standard repulsion parameter), r_c = 1, k_BT = 1, m = 1
"reduced units" + "implicit solvent" + "primitive model"

benchmark_equations.coulomb: \beta u_C(r) = \ell_B\,q_iq_j/r with \ell_B \equiv e^2/(4\pi\varepsilon_0\varepsilon_r k_BT); equivalently u_C(r) = q_iq_j\ell_B/r in k_BT units. The 4\pi is absorbed into \ell_B.
benchmark_equations.gauss_law: \nabla^2\psi = -4\pi\ell_B\,\rho_q (Poisson–Boltzmann in Bjerrum units) — note the 4\pi survives explicitly here even though the Coulomb form has none, because \ell_B is defined with the 4\pi absorbed.

systems.notes: The Coulomb/Gauss pair here is a genuinely instructive inconsistency: the pair potential shows no 4\pi but Poisson's equation shows 4\pi, precisely because \ell_B carries the 4\pi. Any converter that infers 'rationalized vs unrationalized' from a single displayed equation will get this wrong. The elimination of the current dimension I in favour of a length is the sharpest example in this family of a per-paper declaration collapsing the dimension basis.

systems.name: Hamiltonian and classical-chaos conventions (m = ω = 1, Lyapunov-time rescaling)
systems.used_in: nonlinear dynamics, classical and quantum chaos, celestial-mechanics stability studies, Hamiltonian normal-form theory

generators.tex: \omega\ (\text{a chosen mode frequency, orbital frequency, or }\lambda_\text{max})

per_symbol_rescalings.relation: 'time in units of the orbital period T' vs 'in units of \Omega^{-1}': T = 2\pi/\Omega
per_symbol_rescalings.why: the 2\pi. Chaos papers routinely quote both; a Lyapunov exponent quoted 'per orbit' differs from one 'per time unit' by 2\pi

per_symbol_rescalings.relation: Lyapunov time t_\lambda = 1/\lambda_\text{max} used as the time generator; also 'e-folding times' vs 'doubling times' (\ln 2)
per_symbol_rescalings.why: \ln 2 is another invisible numeric factor; and \lambda is itself an OUTPUT, so declaring t_\lambda = 1 makes the unit depend on the result

per_symbol_rescalings.relation: 'we set m = 1' for a multi-particle system means all masses equal, not a unit choice
per_symbol_rescalings.why: only ONE mass can be absorbed into units; setting every m_i = 1 is a physical restriction (equal masses) masquerading as a convention

per_symbol_rescalings.relation: same for multi-mode systems: setting \omega_1 = 1 is a unit choice; setting \omega_1=\omega_2=1 fixes a resonance
per_symbol_rescalings.why: identical failure mode in the frequency sector; the residues are the frequency RATIOS \omega_2/\omega_1

fingerprints: "we set m = \omega = \hbar = 1 throughout"; "for convenience we take unit mass"
H = \tfrac12(p_x^2+p_y^2) + \tfrac12(x^2+y^2) + x^2y - \tfrac13y^3 (Hénon–Heiles with all constants unity; critical escape energy E = 1/6)
standard map p' = p + K\sin\theta, \theta' = \theta + p' — fully dimensionless, K the only parameter
"times are given in units of the Lyapunov time"; "we integrate for 10^4 orbital periods"
billiards: "unit area", "the boundary has unit perimeter", velocity set to 1

benchmark_equations.coulomb: N/A in general; Coulomb-billiard and hydrogen-in-a-field chaos papers use atomic units instead (a different family).
benchmark_equations.gauss_law: N/A: no field equations.
benchmark_equations.einstein_field: N/A, except for geodesic-flow chaos studies, which use geometrized units plus a curvature-scale generator (e.g. 'we set the AdS radius \ell = 1' or 'the black-hole mass M = 1').
benchmark_equations.schrodinger_or_dirac: Quantum-chaos papers write i\partial_t\psi = (-\tfrac12\nabla^2 + V)\psi with \hbar = m = 1, and then treat \hbar_\text{eff} as a free small parameter — a DIMENSIONLESS residue built from the same symbol that was set to 1, which is a genuine ambiguity for an automated reader.

systems.notes: Two structural warnings that generalize beyond this entry. (1) Many chaos models (standard map, logistic map, tent map, coupled-map lattices) have NO dimensional preimage at all: the dimension basis has rank 0 and there is nothing to restore. The tool should detect and say so rather than invent units. (2) 'm=\omega=\hbar=1' plus a separately-tracked '\hbar_eff' is a real convention in quantum chaos in which the SAME symbol is both a generator and a residue; this needs an explicit UI affordance (a symbol can be declared 'absorbed' in one role and 'free parameter' in another).

systems.name: Lattice-model condensed-matter units (a = ħ = t = 1)
systems.used_in: Hubbard/t–J/Heisenberg model papers, DMRG/QMC/DMFT numerics, topological-band-structure literature

generators.tex: e\ (\text{when a flux or field is present})

per_symbol_rescalings.relation: H = -J\sum_{\langle ij\rangle}s_is_j with s=\pm1 versus H = -J\sum \mathbf{S}_i\cdot\mathbf{S}_j with S=\pm\tfrac12: the two 'J = 1' differ by a factor of 4
per_symbol_rescalings.why: a pure numeric factor; it moves the 2D Ising T_c between 2.269 and 0.567 in 'units of J'

per_symbol_rescalings.relation: 'energies in units of t' versus 'in units of the bandwidth W = 4t (1D), 8t (2D square), 12t (3D cubic)'
per_symbol_rescalings.why: DMFT papers overwhelmingly use W or the half-bandwidth D = W/2; Hubbard-model papers use t. U/t = 8 and U/W = 1 are the same physics.

per_symbol_rescalings.relation: magnetic flux per plaquette in units of the flux quantum \Phi_0 = h/e (or hc/e in Gaussian, or h/2e for superconductors)
per_symbol_rescalings.why: three different flux quanta differing by 2 and by c

per_symbol_rescalings.relation: crystal momentum in units of 1/a, with the Brillouin zone [-\pi,\pi] rather than [-\pi/a,\pi/a]
per_symbol_rescalings.why: the \pi's are structural, but papers that set a = 2\pi or use [-1/2,1/2] reduced coordinates exist

fingerprints: "we set \hbar = a = 1 and measure energies in units of the hopping t"
dispersion displayed as \epsilon(k) = -2(\cos k_x + \cos k_y) with no a and no t
"U/t = 8", "J/t", "we take t = 1 as the energy unit"
"temperatures are in units of t" (i.e. k_B = 1)
band structures with the BZ labelled \Gamma, X, M and k running over [-\pi,\pi]

benchmark_equations.coulomb: Usually replaced by an on-site/nearest-neighbour Hubbard term U n_\uparrow n_\downarrow + V n_in_j, with U and V given as ratios to t. Where long-range Coulomb is kept, it appears as (U/t)\,/\,|i-j| in lattice units — the 4\pi\varepsilon_0 is absorbed into the single number U.
benchmark_equations.gauss_law: N/A for lattice models; the electromagnetic sector enters only through Peierls phases \exp(i\frac{e}{\hbar}\!\int\! A\cdot dl) \to \exp(i\theta_{ij}) with the flux measured in \Phi_0.
benchmark_equations.schrodinger_or_dirac: i\,\partial_t c_j = -\sum_{\delta} c_{j+\delta} + \ldots ; continuum Dirac-cone limit written as H = v_F(\sigma_xk_x+\sigma_yk_y) with v_F = 3ta/2\hbar \to 3/2, or with the further declaration v_F = 1.

systems.notes: Five generators over five dimensions once e is included — a complete basis. The dangerous content is entirely in numeric_factor: the spin-1/2 versus Ising factor of 4, the hopping-vs-bandwidth factor of 4–12, and the flux-quantum factor of 2. Note also 'v_F = 1' in Dirac-material papers, which is a SECOND velocity generator layered on top of a=\hbar=t=1 and is therefore over-determined unless one of the others is released — a rank violation the tool should catch.

systems.name: Harmonic-trap units (BEC / Gross–Pitaevskii)
systems.used_in: Bose–Einstein condensate theory and simulation, Gross–Pitaevskii solvers, cold-atom many-body papers

per_symbol_rescalings.relation: length unit a_\text{ho} = \sqrt{\hbar/(m\omega)}; note the absence of a factor 2 — but the oscillator GROUND-STATE width is a_\text{ho}/\sqrt2
per_symbol_rescalings.why: 'the oscillator length' is used for both, a factor \sqrt2

per_symbol_rescalings.relation: \hat g = 4\pi N a_s/a_\text{ho} when \int|\psi|^2 = 1; \hat g = 4\pi a_s/a_\text{ho} when \int|\psi|^2 = N
per_symbol_rescalings.why: the factor N moves between the coupling and the normalization; the two conventions are equally common and dimensionally identical

per_symbol_rescalings.relation: which \omega is the generator: \omega_\perp (quasi-1D/2D papers), \omega_z, or the geometric mean \omega_\text{ho}
per_symbol_rescalings.why: anisotropy ratios \lambda = \omega_z/\omega_\perp are the residues; picking the wrong generator rescales every length by \sqrt\lambda

fingerprints: "lengths in units of the oscillator length a_\text{ho} = \sqrt{\hbar/m\omega}, energies in \hbar\omega, time in \omega^{-1}"
GPE displayed as i\partial_t\psi = \big(-\tfrac12\nabla^2 + \tfrac12(x^2+y^2+\lambda^2z^2) + g|\psi|^2\big)\psi
the combination Na_s/a_\text{ho} quoted as the interaction parameter
"Thomas–Fermi radius R_\text{TF} = (15Na_s/a_\text{ho})^{1/5}" (in trap units)

benchmark_equations.coulomb: N/A: neutral atoms; dipolar BEC papers introduce \epsilon_{dd} = a_{dd}/a_s, a dimensionless residue.
benchmark_equations.gauss_law: N/A: no gauge field, except in synthetic-gauge-field papers where the flux is quoted in dimensionless units.
benchmark_equations.einstein_field: N/A: nonrelativistic (analogue-gravity BEC papers introduce an emergent 'c' equal to the sound speed, a second velocity generator).
benchmark_equations.schrodinger_or_dirac: i\,\partial_t\psi = \big(-\tfrac12\nabla^2 + V_\text{ext} + g|\psi|^2\big)\psi, with V_\text{ext} = \tfrac12 r^2 for an isotropic trap and g = 4\pi N a_s/a_\text{ho} for \int|\psi|^2 = 1. The kinetic prefactor is exactly 1/2, not 1 — a frequent transcription error.

systems.notes: Three generators over (M, L, T) — complete and independent. The whole risk is in the coupling constant's numeric factor (4\pi, and whether N is inside g). Worth an explicit UI field: 'wavefunction normalization convention' is a per-paper datum that changes the meaning of g by a factor of N.

systems.name: Optical-lattice recoil units
aliases: lattice depth in units of the recoil energy
systems.used_in: optical-lattice cold-atom experiments and theory, Bose/Fermi–Hubbard parameter derivations, matter-wave diffraction

per_symbol_rescalings.relation: E_R = \hbar^2k_L^2/2m with k_L = 2\pi/\lambda (photon recoil) versus E_R = \hbar^2k^2/2m with k = 2\pi/(\lambda/2) = 2k_L (lattice-period recoil), a factor of 4
per_symbol_rescalings.why: the lattice period is \lambda/2, so both definitions are 'natural'; a lattice depth of '10 E_R' can mean two different physical depths

per_symbol_rescalings.relation: V(x) = V_0\sin^2(k_Lx) versus V(x) = \tfrac{V_0}{2}[1-\cos(2k_Lx)] versus V(x) = -\tfrac{V_0}{2}\cos(2k_Lx): peak-to-peak versus amplitude, a factor of 2
per_symbol_rescalings.why: a pure numeric factor that changes the derived Hubbard t and U substantially because they depend exponentially on \sqrt{s}

per_symbol_rescalings.relation: m is absorbed inside E_R rather than declared separately, so 'the mass' is not an independent generator here
per_symbol_rescalings.why: E_R, \hbar, k_L is a complete independent set and m = \hbar^2k_L^2/(2E_R) is derived — the reverse of the trap-units convention

fingerprints: "the lattice depth is s = V_0/E_R = 12"; "E_R = \hbar^2k^2/2m is the recoil energy"
H/E_R = -\partial_{\tilde x}^2 + s\sin^2(\tilde x) with \tilde x = k_Lx
band structures plotted versus quasimomentum q/\hbar k_L \in [-1,1]
"in units of the recoil"; "E_R/h = 3.5\ \text{kHz}" (frequency-unit restoration)

benchmark_equations.coulomb: N/A: neutral atoms.
benchmark_equations.gauss_law: N/A.
benchmark_equations.schrodinger_or_dirac: In recoil units with x̃ = k_Lx and energies in E_R: \hat H = -\partial_{\tilde x}^2 + s\sin^2\tilde x. Derivation: -\frac{\hbar^2}{2m}\partial_x^2 = -E_R\,\partial_{\tilde x}^2 exactly, because E_R \equiv \hbar^2k_L^2/2m. Note the kinetic prefactor is 1, NOT 1/2 — the opposite of trap units, because the 1/2 was absorbed into E_R.

systems.notes: Instructive contrast with trap units: the same physics (\hbar = m = 1-style) yields a kinetic prefactor of 1 here and 1/2 there, purely because of which numeric factor sat inside the energy generator. This is a strong argument that numeric_factor must be attached to the generator, not to the equation. The \lambda-vs-\lambda/2 recoil ambiguity is a genuine, documented source of confusion in the cold-atom literature.

systems.name: Cavity-QED / circuit-QED and open-system conventions
systems.used_in: cavity and circuit QED, optomechanics, quantum-optics master-equation papers, Jaynes–Cummings and Dicke-model literature

per_symbol_rescalings.relation: H \to UHU^\dagger - iU\partial_tU^\dagger with U = e^{i\omega_d t(a^\dagger a + \sigma_z/2)}, giving detunings \Delta_c = \omega_c-\omega_d
per_symbol_rescalings.why: this is an ADDITIVE, time-dependent transformation of the Hamiltonian, not a unit choice at all, yet it is announced in the same breath as '\hbar=1' and it removes \omega_c from every displayed equation

per_symbol_rescalings.relation: H_\text{int} = g(a\sigma_+ + a^\dagger\sigma_-) versus \tfrac{\Omega}{2}(\ldots) with \Omega = 2g (vacuum Rabi frequency = 2g, vacuum Rabi splitting = 2g)
per_symbol_rescalings.why: factor-of-2 conventions between coupling, Rabi frequency and splitting; all reported as 'the coupling'

per_symbol_rescalings.relation: \mathcal{D}[a] with rate \kappa (energy decay) versus \kappa/2 (amplitude decay); linewidth (FWHM) = \kappa
per_symbol_rescalings.why: factor-of-2 ambiguity in every quoted cooperativity C = g^2/(\kappa\gamma) versus 4g^2/(\kappa\gamma)

fingerprints: "we set \hbar = 1" immediately followed by a Hamiltonian in angular-frequency units
"all rates are given in units of \kappa" / "in units of g" / "energies are measured in units of the cavity linewidth"
H = \omega_ca^\dagger a + \tfrac{\omega_a}{2}\sigma_z + g(a\sigma_+ + a^\dagger\sigma_-) (Jaynes–Cummings, \hbar=1)
cooperativity C = g^2/(\kappa\gamma) or 2g^2/(\kappa\gamma) quoted as the figure of merit
"in the frame rotating at the drive frequency"

benchmark_equations.coulomb: N/A: the light–matter coupling is already reduced to a dipole matrix element folded into g.
benchmark_equations.gauss_law: N/A: the field is a single quantized mode; no field equation is displayed.
benchmark_equations.schrodinger_or_dirac: i\,\partial_t|\psi\rangle = H|\psi\rangle with \hbar=1, or the Lindblad form \dot\rho = -i[H,\rho] + \kappa\mathcal{D}[a]\rho + \gamma\mathcal{D}[\sigma_-]\rho. With \hbar=1 every 'energy' in the paper is an angular frequency, and the conversion to laboratory numbers usually goes through h (not \hbar): 'g/2\pi = 100\ \text{MHz}'.

systems.notes: Only ONE genuine dimensional generator beyond \hbar (a frequency), so the dimensional content is thin; nearly all the convention risk here is factor-of-2 and factor-of-2\pi (the ubiquitous 'g/2\pi = ...' means the quoted number is an ordinary frequency while the symbol is angular). Rotating frames are the clearest case in the whole family of a transformation that a units engine must recognize and REFUSE to model as a unit change.

systems.name: Fermi units (ħ = k_F = 1, with m or E_F set to 1)
systems.used_in: ultracold Fermi gases and the BCS–BEC crossover, nuclear matter, Fermi-liquid theory, quantum Monte Carlo of the electron gas

generators.tex: m\ \text{or}\ E_F\ (\text{third generator; only one may be chosen})

per_symbol_rescalings.relation: E_F = \hbar^2k_F^2/(2m). Choosing \hbar=k_F=m=1 forces E_F = 1/2. Choosing \hbar=k_F=E_F=1 forces m = 1/2.
per_symbol_rescalings.why: derived here explicitly. Both declarations appear in the literature and BOTH are dimensionally complete (the 3x3 exponent matrix for (\hbar,k_F,E_F) has determinant 1), so a dimension check cannot distinguish them — only the factor-of-2 in every reported energy does.

systems.notes: THE structural failure case, and the reason I recommend an explicit 'unsupported' verdict rather than a heroic extension. h is DIMENSIONLESS: its exponent tuple is (0,0,0,0,0), so it contributes a zero row to the restoration matrix and carries no dimensional trace whatsoever. Restoration of h-factors is therefore not a linear-algebra problem over dimensions at all — it requires a per-quantity lookup table of h-exponents. The same objection applies to any declaration of the form 'we set [dimensionless quantity] = 1' (Re = 1, \alpha = 1, \hbar_\text{eff} = 1, m_i/m_e = 25). The honest tool behavior is to DETECT such a declaration, refuse to fold it into the generator table, and surface it as an un-restorable annotation on the affected symbols. A v2 feature could ship a curated h-exponent table for the ~20 standard cosmological observables.

family_notes:
VERDICT. The generator-table formalism does extend to per-paper nondimensionalization, but only after four schema additions; without them the extension is unsound rather than merely incomplete.

(1) Generators must be allowed to be FREE SYMBOLS, not constants of nature. A user/mined generator is a triple (tex, dimension 5-tuple, optional SI value). The dimension tuple is what the restoration linear system needs and is always known symbolically from the declaration sentence ("lengths are scaled by L", "velocities by U"); the SI value is needed only for round-tripping to physical numbers and is frequently absent from the paper entirely (scale-free simulations: ideal GRMHD, vacuum NR, LJ MD). So the tool must support restoration WITHOUT numeric values — emitting "L", "U", "\\rho_0" symbolically — and treat numeric values as an optional overlay. Roughly half the systems above are published without them.

(2) A RANK CHECK is mandatory and is the single highest-value new feature. In fixed systems (ħ=c=G=1) the generators are known-independent. In per-paper scaling they very often are not. Three distinct outcomes must be distinguished: (a) rank = number of active base dimensions and generator count equals rank — well-posed, unique restoration (LJ units, NS inertial scaling, Hénon units, trap units); (b) generator count exceeds rank — OVER-DETERMINED, and the excess declarations are physical restrictions disguised as unit choices ("L = U = ν = 1" secretly means Re = 1; "m_i = 1 for all i" means equal masses; "a = ħ = t = v_F = 1" in Dirac-material papers is a rank violation). The tool should compute the null-space combination that has been silently set to 1 and name it; (c) generator count is below rank — PARTIAL nondimensionalization, leaving residual dimensional freedom, which is common and legitimate (nuclear matter in ħ=c=1 with k_F still in fm^-1). Note the important exception in the GRMHD entry: two same-dimension mass generators are consistent there only because ideal GRMHD has an exact density-scaling symmetry, so the rank check must be overridable with a flag "generator exploits an equation symmetry" rather than hard-failing.

(3) BASIS REDUCTION must be modeled explicitly. Several declarations do not scale a dimension, they delete it: k_B = 1 removes Θ (LJ, gyrokinetics, lattice models), μ0 = 1 or absorption into the Bjerrum length removes I (MHD codes, soft matter), c = 1 merges L and T. The active-basis state is therefore part of the convention record, and translating between two conventions with different active bases (e.g. a compressible-CFD paper with Θ live and an MD paper with Θ dead) requires re-inflating the basis, not just multiplying quotients.

(4) RESIDUES must be a first-class output, and must never be restored. The defining feature of this family, versus fixed unit systems, is that the surviving dimensionless groups — Re, Pr, Ra, Ma, Ek, Ro, St, Pe, Sc, S, Pr_m, β, ρ*, ν*, σ, N (soliton order), U/t, ℓ_B/σ, 1/k_F a, s = V0/E_R, C = g²/κγ, m_i/m_e — are physics, not units. A restoration engine that treats them as absorbable constants produces nonsense. The correct output of the engine on a per-paper convention is: {generator list} + {Buckingham Π basis of the null space, labeled against a registry of named groups}. A curated residue registry (name, definition, field) is a modest, high-value data asset.

UI / DATA THE TOOL NEEDS. A per-document "scale declaration" panel with one row per declared scale: TeX symbol; dimension 5-tuple (entered directly, or inferred from a defining expression like sqrt(g α ΔT H), which the tool can dimension-check); numeric factor (the 2π, √2, 1/2, 4π, −1/4 that dimensional analysis cannot see); optional SI value; and a three-way classifier {unit generator | symmetry parameter | physical restriction}. Plus: an active-basis widget showing which of (M,L,T,Θ,I) survive; a computed rank/nullity readout with the Π-basis named; a per-symbol rider table for definitional rescalings (B_code = B/√(4π); v_th = √(2T/m) vs √(T/m); ψ normalized to 1 vs N; T_FWHM vs T_0); and a convention-to-convention translator that composes two per-paper tables and reports the answer as powers of named residues (the RBC free-fall ↔ diffusive map is exactly a power of √(Ra Pr)). Preset library: the named conventions above, shipped as editable templates, since most papers use a standard one with one or two switches flipped (GENE with L_ref = a vs R_0; Boussinesq free-fall vs diffusive; recoil energy at λ vs λ/2).

FINGERPRINTING THE DECLARATION SENTENCE. High-precision cues, roughly in order of reliability: (i) a normalization TABLE in the methods section, two columns, rows like "length | L_ref", "time | L_ref/c_ref" — this is the single strongest signal and is machine-extractable; (ii) explicit declarative templates — /we (work|shall work|will work) in units (in )?(which|where)/, /we set ([^.]{1,80}) = 1/, /(all )?(lengths|times|energies|velocities|frequencies|masses) are (measured |given |expressed )?in units of/, /normalized (to|by)/, /we adopt the following normali[sz]ation/, /(reduced|code|internal|natural|dimensionless) units/, /for convenience( we| ,)/, /henceforth/, /unless otherwise (stated|noted)/; (iii) decorated variables plus a legend — /(hats?|tildes?|primes?|asterisks?|stars?) denote (the )?(dimensionless|normali[sz]ed|reduced)/, followed later by /we drop the (hats|tildes|primes)/, which is the point after which every subsequent equation is in-system; (iv) named dimensionless groups appearing as bare coefficients on displayed PDE terms; (v) a restoration appendix — /to convert to (physical|cgs|SI) units/, /multiplying by/, a table of unit values; (vi) code-specific keyword leakage ("units lj", "UnitLength_in_cm", "M_unit", "tprim/fprim", "\\Omega = 1"). A useful two-stage extractor: regex-locate the declaration paragraph, then LLM-parse it into (symbol, defining expression, dimension) triples, then dimension-CHECK each defining expression against the claimed role and show the user any mismatch before committing the convention.

FAILURE MODES TO FLAG (ranked by how often they actually bite).
- Partial nondimensionalization. "We set c = ħ = 1 but quote lengths in fm"; "energies in eV, lengths in lattice units". Very common, entirely legitimate, and fatal to any engine that assumes a declaration is total. Detect by rank < basis size and warn rather than fail.
- Inconsistent / over-declared scales. Papers that list more unit-fixing statements than there are dimensions. Almost always the author means "and additionally the relevant dimensionless group equals 1", which is a physical claim. Compute and display the implied group.
- Section-local conventions. A single paper using linear theory in ω_ce units, simulations in code units, and observations in SI, with no explicit switch marker. Neutron-star papers routinely combine Fermi units (EOS) with geometrized units (TOV) in adjacent equations. The tool's convention state must be scoped to a text span, not to a document.
- Silent per-symbol redefinition. The symbol looks the same, the dimension is the same, the meaning is not: B → B/√(4π), v_th with or without √2, ψ normalized to 1 or N, g vs Ω/2, κ vs κ/2, J for s=±1 vs S=±1/2, hopping t vs bandwidth W. Dimension checking is blind to all of these; only the numeric_factor/rider tables catch them.
- The 2π/ln2 class. Box side 1 vs 2π, period vs angular frequency, orbits vs Ω^-1, e-folding vs doubling times, "g/2π = 100 MHz". Same dimension, different number.
- Dimensionless "units". Little-h, "units where Re = 1", α = 1, ħ_eff. No dimensional trace exists; restoration is impossible in principle. Detect and annotate; do not attempt.
- Equations with no dimensional preimage. Standard map, logistic map, coupled-map lattices, abstract dynamical systems: rank 0, nothing to restore. Say so rather than inventing units.
- Non-multiplicative "normalizations" announced alongside real ones. Additive temperature offsets θ = (T − T_ref)/ΔT in Boussinesq; co-moving/retarded frames in NLS; rotating frames in quantum optics; comoving-vs-physical coordinates with a time-dependent a(t) in cosmological codes. These are affine or time-dependent transformations, outside the multiplicative generator group entirely; the tool must recognize and refuse them rather than mis-modeling them.
- Scales that are not actually free. "M = 1" is a genuine symmetry in vacuum NR and a mere reported number in BNS/matter NR; "density is scale-free" holds in ideal GRMHD but not once radiative cooling fixes a density. A warning triggered by the co-presence of a fixed-scale ingredient (an EOS, a cooling function, a real collision frequency) alongside a claimed free scale would catch a real class of physics errors.
- Deliberately unphysical residues. Reduced ion-to-electron mass ratios (25, 64, 100), reduced speed of light, inflated resistivity. Dimensionally invisible, and a restoration engine must never "correct" them to physical values.

SCOPE RECOMMENDATION. v1: the custom-generator engine itself (symbolic generators, rank check, residue extraction, basis reduction) plus presets for the handful of conventions a theoretical-physics reader meets constantly — NS inertial scaling, LJ reduced units, m=ω=ħ=1 Hamiltonian/chaos, NR G=c=M=1, lattice a=ħ=t=1, trap units. v2: the domain presets (Boussinesq ×2, Alfvénic MHD, both gyrokinetic families, PIC, shearing box, Hénon, recoil, Fermi, NLS, code-unit triples, GRMHD) plus the convention-to-convention translator and the named-residue registry. Out of scope for restoration, in scope for detection-and-warning: dimensionless-generator declarations (h-units and friends), affine/rotating-frame transformations, and models with no dimensional preimage.
